title: Role lookup fallback priority race results in dual permission states
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A production customer (finance vertical) reported two behavior classes happening within minutes: (1) immediate permission denied errors for workspace admins after a large SAML group sync finished, and (2) subsequent requests from the same identities were accepted with elevated privileges (admin + extra service roles). Both phenomena correlate with a large group-sync job and a concurrent user API activity spike.

Observed behavior:
- t0: SAML group sync starts (syncing ~12k group mappings).
- t0 + ~30s: several admin users report 403 when hitting admin console endpoints.
- t0 + ~2m: same identities can perform admin actions and also access restricted service routes that should be deny-only for their roles.
- Audit logs show a brief window where the RBAC decision engine returns DENY, followed by ALLOW decisions that include roles merged from both SAML group assignment and cached service-token grants.

Reproduction steps (dev env):
1) Spin a test org with RBAC v2 enabled and SAML group mapping to roles.
2) Seed 10k group mappings and 3 heavy background sync cycles.
3) Fire concurrent admin-console requests while triggering sync.
4) Observe transient 403s followed by ALLOWs with expanded role set for same user session.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Fallback lookup priority when evaluating a principal consults (A) role bindings cache, (B) live SAML-claims resolver, (C) service-token grants.
- During heavy SAML sync, the claims resolver intermittently returns partial group sets (race between delta application and the claims cache invalidation). Requests hitting the service between cache eviction and final delta application hit an internal fast-path that marks the principal as "unknown -> deny" then writes a new binding on reconciliation.
- A separate merge path incorrectly unions the resolved role list from the background reconciliation with an ephemeral service-token grant without de-duplicating deny/allow semantics, leading to an over-permissioned ALLOW state.
- Audit logging metadata for the initial DENY loses the correlation_id because the deny path uses an optimistic short-lived request ID; when the final ALLOW is recorded the final decision points to the new binding without a clean link to the initial decision.

Proposed fix:
1) Change role-lookup priority to: (1) authoritative binding store read (strong read), (2) claims resolver (strong read with in-flight sync lock), (3) service-token grants. Avoid using stale cache entries for initial decision when a sync is in progress.
2) During SAML sync window, hold a reconciliation lock per-org that serializes binding writes and prevents fast-path optimistic denies from materializing. The lock is lightweight (per-org, ttl 30s, exponential backoff).
3) Harden merge logic to enforce idempotent role unions and enforce explicit deny precedence: any previously-recorded deny flags on a principal must be re-evaluated and recorded in audit metadata.
4) Preserve correlation_id across deny->allow transitions by threading original request id through reconciliation tasks.

Mitigation (short-term):
- For affected customers, disable parallel SAML delta application (admin toggle) and increase claims-cache TTL to 30s to reduce race surface.
- Provide a temporary rule in console to force read-through to authoritative binding store for admin routes.

Telemetry & logs to gather:
- Sampling of request traces that show decision path for both DENY and ALLOW for same principal within 5 minutes.
- SAML-sync job timings, chunk sizes, and last-applied-delta id.
- audit.log entries with correlation_id, old_bindings, new_bindings, and decision_path tag.

Backwards compatibility considerations:
- The reconciliation lock adds a small serialization point during large org syncs; documented as potential 1–3s extra sync time for large orgs.
- No change to API surface; only decision engine internal ordering and audit enrichment.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests covering race (mock sync + concurrent auth requests) pass deterministically in CI.
- End-to-end test that reproduces prior repro no longer shows transient DENY->OVERGRANT for same principal within 10 minutes in staging.
- Audit logs contain stable correlation_ids and show a single canonical decision per request with full before/after binding snapshots.
- Rollout plan with feature flag (rbac-v2-reconciliation-lock) and canary 1% -> 25% -> 100% in Dedicated regions.

References:
- Internal PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2415
- Customer escalation thread (redacted): https://company.slack.com/archives/C0245EXAMPLE/p1676480000000100
